sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup
sections.what: Imports the hashing and file-reading tools, the test tools, and the calibration functions. Reads from a fixed relative path for the data.
sections.why: Gives the tests what they need to load the saved file and rerun the calculations.
sections.watch_out: The data path is relative. Running the tests from another folder will fail to find the file.

sections.name: Season, samples
sections.title: Saved record shape and sample loader
sections.what: Describes the shape of each season's saved record and loads the file. Builds a flat list of per-ball samples for a chosen prediction method, so the statistics can be rerun.
sections.why: The statistical functions need one flat list of predictions, and the saved file stores them per match.
sections.watch_out: Field names must match the saved file exactly, or the checks fail for reasons that look unrelated.

sections.name: rolling-origin calibration gate on real seasons (calibration)
sections.title: Rolling-origin gate checks
sections.what: Checks the file hash. Checks that tuning used only 2024 and that each season's fit used only the three seasons before it. Checks that the predictions reproduce each season's verdict, bucket counts, ECE and Brier scores. Checks that the recorded result is a failure with the 2026 drift and that no fairness variant passes.
sections.why: Likely reason: the owner wants the saved verdict reproduced exactly, including the failure, rather than tuned away.
sections.watch_out: The gate settings in the test, such as the minimum matches, bootstrap count and maximum ECE, must match the script that made the file. Changing them alone changes the reproduced values.

summary: Checks a saved record of how a win-probability calibration model was tested season by season, and confirms that the saved result records a failure honestly.
purpose: Makes sure the rolling-origin calibration result can be reproduced from its stored predictions and that its failing verdict is not hidden.
why: The comments say this is the owner's decision D-027, run on Cricsheet IPL data, so the test protects that recorded decision.
how: Loads the JSON results file, checks its content hash, checks the tuning and season split, recomputes the calibration test and Brier scores from the stored predictions, and checks the saved pass or fail values and the fairness results.
inputs: data/models/calibration-v2.json and the matchCalibration engine functions.
outputs: Pass or fail. The test does not write files.
risks: The test assumes the JSON was made by its matching script. If the data is regenerated, the hash and expected verdicts change. The failing expectations are intentional.
debug: If the hash check fails, the file was edited or regenerated without the matching script. If a reproduction check fails, compare the recalculated Brier or ECE value with the stored one for that season.
